session.question: What does the ClinicalTrials.gov record say about the DECISION phase III study design, treatment schedule, endpoints, and trial registration identifier?
session.answer:
The DECISION phase III study is a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial aimed at evaluating the efficacy of sorafenib in patients with locally advanced or metastatic radioactive iodine (RAI)-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC) (unknownauthorsUnknownyearrationaleanddesign chunk 1). The treatment schedule involves administering sorafenib until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity manifests, with efficacy assessments conducted every 56 days and safety evaluations every 28 days during the initial phase (unknownauthorsUnknownyearrationaleanddesign chunk 1).

The primary endpoint of the study is progression-free survival (PFS), while secondary endpoints include overall survival (OS), time to disease progression, disease control rate, and safety (unknownauthorsUnknownyearrationaleanddesign chunk 1). This comprehensive endpoint design addresses both short-term and long-term treatment effects. 

The trial is officially registered with ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier NCT00984282 and EudraCT number 2009-012007-25, ensuring transparency and accessibility for ongoing monitoring of the study’s progress and outcomes (unknownauthorsUnknownyearrationaleanddesign chunk 1). The structure and design emphasize rigorous evaluation of sorafenib's efficacy and safety in a challenging patient population, reflecting contemporary clinical trial standards.
